sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Quality Checks row 51 and Internal Quality Checks row 51; both rubric sheets enumerated
evidence: Frozen workbook Quality Checks row 51 asks whether task.toml, scoring.toml, all judge.toml files, shell scripts and reference entry parse. Independent checks in per-row-review/evidence/51/checks.json parsed all 7 TOML files, all 4 frozen JSON files including environment/assets/seed_data.json, both Python helper sources via ast.parse, and the reference app JavaScript entry solution/app/server.js via node --check; no parse errors. Both solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh passed bash -n (exit 0) and byte checks found neither CRLF nor bare CR. The generated restart-shell heredoc also passed bash -n; all three Python heredocs in test.sh parsed, as did the Node heredoc in solve.sh. Other first-party JavaScript passed node --check; src/vendor.js uses ESM exports imported by src/app.tsx:1 and the module script at solution/app/index.html:1, so its CommonJS-mode node --check error is a mode mismatch; node --check --input-type=module passed on its exact bytes. The frozen manifest's 43 task and 34 rule hashes match current bytes; all 77 raw-index artifact hashes match. Indexed attempt2/full-install-binding.json independently binds the exact frozen solution files to an actual solve.sh install, a running node /app/server.js, and HTTP 200 from /api/health. This is scripted golden startup evidence, not a full configured judge, Oracle, target-model or portal grade. A syntactically valid static or dead app could pass this row while failing product checks; conversely, a conforming browser ESM source would be falsely rejected by a CommonJS-only syntax probe, which is why the ESM mode was checked. Required full configured judge evidence remains absent, so risk stays true.
